To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Any list, spreadsheet, tracker or summary of the contracts, task orders, grants or other agreements that were terminated, partially terminated, descoped or not renewed under the Secretary of Defense's memo of March 13, 2025, which directed the termination of "all ONA contracts awarded for ONA and ONA-related requirements." For each, this would ideally show the contractor, contract or task-order number, project title, obligated value, value at termination, and termination date.
2. Termination notices, stop-work orders, termination-for-convenience settlement proposals, and settlement agreements or modifications for those contracts.
3. Records identifying deliverables (studies, reports, assessments, workshops or other products) that were unfinished, partially completed or undelivered when their contracts were terminated. This includes any partial or draft deliverables the government received when the contracts ended.
4. Records showing estimated or actual savings, termination costs and settlement payments from the ONA contract terminations.
5. Communications about which ONA contracts to terminate, keep or exempt. This includes communications with the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment and with the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) or anyone acting for it.

Search instructions: Please search ONA's records, the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment, the Washington Headquarters Services Acquisition Directorate, and any other contracting activity that awarded or administered ONA contracts. If records are held by another DoD component's contracting office, please refer the request to that office and tell me which one.

If any responsive records were destroyed or transferred, please include records showing when, how and under whose authority.

For anything withheld, please cite the exemption for each redaction. For classified material, please give the classification level, the classification authority and the declassification date. Please release all pages, even heavily redacted ones, with administrative markings and pagination intact.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. The plan the Deputy Secretary of Defense was directed to give the Secretary of Defense within 30 days to rebuild or reconstitute the Office of Net Assessment (ONA), under the Secretary's memo of March 13, 2025. This includes all drafts, versions, attachments and briefing slides.
2. Any transmittal memos, cover notes or decision memos that came with the plan, and any record of the Secretary's approval, disapproval, changes or other action on it.
3. Any later directives, charters, DoD directives or instructions, organizational charts, staffing plans or mission statements for a reconstituted ONA or any successor office.
4. Records showing ONA's staffing and budget before and after the March 13, 2025, memo. This includes the number of authorized and filled positions and ONA's budget in each fiscal year from FY2024 through FY2026.
5. Emails and other communications about the rebuild plan or ONA's reconstitution among the Office of the Secretary of Defense, the Office of the Deputy Secretary of Defense, the Director of Administration and Management, the Performance Improvement Officer, and ONA staff or leadership.

Please search the Office of the Secretary of Defense, the Office of the Deputy Secretary of Defense (including its front office and Executive Secretariat), the Director of Administration and Management, and the Performance Improvement Officer. Please follow any leads to other offices or record systems.

If no plan was ever produced, please say so in your response and provide records showing that, such as tasking trackers or suspense logs for the 30-day deadline.

For anything withheld, please cite the exemption for each redaction. For classified material, please give the classification level, the classification authority and the declassification date. Please release all pages, even heavily redacted ones, with administrative markings and pagination intact.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Any index, list, catalog, log or database of the reports, studies, assessments, summer study products, workshop reports and other final deliverables that ONA produced, commissioned or received from 1 January 2015 to 1 April 2025. For each item, this would ideally show its title, date, author or performing contractor, contract or task-order number, and classification level.

If no single index exists, records showing the same information, such as deliverable tracking logs, annual or periodic reports to the Secretary of Defense summarizing ONA's research, or reading lists of completed studies.

Records showing every contract, grant, task order or other agreement that ONA awarded or funded, including the contractor, project title, period of performance, obligated amount, and whether the work was classified.

The Department has released this kind of record before. An index of ONA reports covering roughly two decades was released under FOIA and reported by Talking Points Memo. This request seeks the equivalent records for the years since.
Please search ONA's files and any office that received ONA's records when ONA's staff were reassigned and its contracts ended after the Secretary's memo of March 13, 2025. That includes the Office of the Director of Administration and Management and the contracting offices that managed ONA awards. Please follow any leads to other record systems. If any responsive records were destroyed or transferred, please include records showing when, how and under whose authority.

Under the foreseeable-harm standard in 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(8)(A), information may be withheld only where disclosure would foreseeably harm an interest protected by an exemption. I expect most entries in an index of study titles, dates and contractors to be unclassified and releasable. If some titles are classified, please redact them line by line and release the rest of the index rather than withholding it entirely.

For anything withheld, please cite the exemption for each redaction. For classified material, please give the classification level, the classification authority and the declassification date. Please release all pages, even heavily redacted ones, with administrative markings and pagination intact.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

In CSV/excel format, roster information for all officers who have been employed by Boston Police Department since June 2025.

Some important fields may include:
- City of Boston Employee ID (6-digit ID)
- Badge Number
- Officer First, Middle, Last Name
- Officer Rank
- Sex, race, age if available
- Officer Photo

If any portion of this request is exempt, I request all segregable non-exempt data fields be released.

I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2020) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f). 

Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents. 

I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations.

If you do not waive the fees associated with my request, please provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate and explanation of the fees prior to fulfilling my request. See 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.0792)(b); see also ch. 66, § 10(e) (“A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days.”). 

If you believe any of the records I have requested are exempt from disclosure, please identify both: (1) the records, categories of records, or portions of the records you intend to withhold; and (2) the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption you are relying on. See ch. 66, § 10(b)(iv).

If necessary to comply with my request, I welcome your suggested modifications pursuant to ch. 66, § 10(b)(vii) and 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.06(2)(g). I am available to discuss any proposed modifications at (781) 915-8324 or adasuss@bu.edu.

Thank you in advance for your time and attention to this matter. I look forward to receiving your response within 10 business days. See ch. 66, § 10(a).

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

ada sussman

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the The Kansas Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting incident-level crime data for a research project comparing neighborhood-level crime across large US cities. I am asking for the same kind of extract many departments already publish through their open data portals.

Records requested. One row per reported offense, for offenses occurring between 1 January 2019 and 31 December 2025, with these fields:

the incident, case or report number
the date the offense occurred
the offense description, and the offense code if you have one
the location of the offense, as latitude and longitude

Offense fields. Whatever your system already stores is fine. Something along the lines of NIBRS offense codes and descriptions is ideal, but please do not translate, recode or reclassify anything on my behalf. I am not asking you to do any work beyond exporting the fields as they sit. If your records hold more than one offense description or classification per record (for example a local code, a UCR or NIBRS code, and a plain-text description), please include all of them rather than choosing between them.

Location. If coordinates cannot be released, I will accept a block-level address instead - either "4200 BLOCK OF WYOMING ST" or an address with the house number masked to the hundred block, for example "42XX WYOMING ST". I am not asking for exact street addresses. Several large departments publish location in exactly this masked form, and it is sufficient for my purposes.

No personal information is requested. I am not asking for the name, address, date of birth, race, sex, age or any other identifying detail of any victim, witness, suspect, arrestee or officer. Please withhold all such fields. I am asking only for what the offense was, when it happened, and roughly where.

Format. CSV, or any delimited or database export your records system produces. One file for the whole period is easiest, but annual files are fine.

Cost. Please send me a written estimate before incurring any charge above $50.

If any part of this cannot be released, please release the rest and tell me what was withheld and why.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jonathan Mummolo

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, I request the following data from the City of Minneapolis 911 computer-aided dispatch (CAD) system. This follows my earlier request DR26_009356, which was closed.

For each record in the City's published OpenData 911 dataset, please provide the following fields, keyed to Master_Incident_Number so they can be joined to that dataset, for the full period the dataset covers:

Case Number (the incident report file number)
Source or call origin (for example 911, non-emergency line, 311, officer or self-initiated), beyond the is_911_Call flag
Call Taker ID and Dispatcher ID
Received, Entry, Dispatch, Enroute, On Scene, and Close date and time
Cancelled indicator (whether the call was cancelled before officer arrival)
Prime Unit and additional responding unit identifiers
Any Program or Response Type field identifying a behavioral health, crisis, or co-response dispatch, separate from the agency-response flags already on OpenData

Field names in the CAD system may differ from mine. I am requesting the functional equivalent of each. If a field does not exist, please say so. Please also provide any existing data dictionary or codebook for these fields, including the value lists for disposition, problem or nature, and any response-type field.
